subject: Biotechnology
title: Virus-Resistant Crops
description: A short lesson to help you apply Virus-Resistant Crops.

hook.text: Papaya ringspot virus nearly destroyed Hawaii's papaya industry — a transgenic papaya saved it.

buildup.text: The Rainbow papaya carries a viral coat protein gene — it triggers RNA silencing against the invading virus.

discovery.text: Pathogen-derived resistance uses the virus's own genes against it — a molecular vaccination for plants.

twist.text: Cassava mosaic virus threatens food security for 800 million people — virus-resistant cassava is in development.

climax.text: RNA interference now protects crops against multiple viruses simultaneously — broad-spectrum plant immunity.

punchline.text: Turn the virus's coat into a shield — transgenic resistance saves harvests.

quiz.question: How does pathogen-derived resistance protect plants?
options: It strengthens plant cell walls to physically block virus entry
A viral gene expressed in the plant triggers RNA silencing against the invading virus
It produces antibodies that neutralize the virus in the soil
